Instant high-quality real time voice and text translation (from services like Skype and Lexifone ) is just about ready for the big-time. Will people still bother to learn other languages when it's so much easier to just have their phone translate? Will cultures become more insular due to not learning others' languages or will they become more cosmopolitan due to being able to easily and efficiently communicate? What unintended effects will this have? Will it prevent or cause conflict?
What will real-time voice translation change about culture and globalization?

I think sharing perspectives is a stronger force for peace than learning the language. If we can share perspectives (with perfect translation) there is almost no need to learn the language. It will lead to more widespread intercultural interaction and help to prevent conflict. People have more in common than not, and breaking down language and cultural barriers prevents people from demonizing other cultures, a necessary step on the road to war.

As tiome goes on and we become more connected, there will be a universal language, and then local dialects and languages, just like how in the roman empire Latin was used universally, and yet other languages began to grow and be created.

Yeah that's why I added "with perfect translation." Idioms and metaphors are problems for translators but I think that neural network (NN) translation is up to the challenge. Existing NN translation models map a phrase through a language net into a "thought vector" from which point it can be passed out through another language net, achieving a semantic translation. I think this model can accommodate idiom translation, so long as the NN is sufficiently complex enough to hold metaphors in a thought vector.
